title: High CPU Usage in Load-Generator Pod Causes Alert
problem: The load-generator pod 'load-generator-5765f7695c-tbstm' in the 'otel-demo' namespace is consuming an abnormally high amount of CPU (about 10.12 cores), causing the container-cpu-high-rate alert to fire. This high consumption has caused previous OOM kills and restarts, indicating instability likely due to resource exhaustion. No error logs were found, so the root cause appears to be related to excessive resource demand rather than a specific fault.
remediations: Investigate the load-generator workload configuration and resource limits to identify causes of high CPU usage.
Adjust resource requests and limits to protect cluster stability.
Review and possibly scale out load generators to distribute CPU load.
Continuously monitor the pod's resource usage to prevent further OOM kills or performance degradation.
raw_diagnosis:
The alert "container-cpu-high-rate" is firing due to a high CPU usage rate detected in the "otel-demo" namespace.

Investigation details:
- Pod status for "load-generator-5765f7695c-tbstm" shows it is running but has had 4 restarts recently with the previous termination reason being "OOMKilled" (out of memory).
- The container CPU usage rate metric (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total[5m])) shows a very high CPU usage for the "load-generator-5765f7695c-tbstm" pod, specifically about 10.12 CPU cores, which is significantly higher than other pods in the namespace.
- No error logs were found in the last hour for the "load-generator-5765f7695c-tbstm" pod.
- All other pods in the "otel-demo" namespace are running with no restarts or CPU usage spikes detected.

Probable root cause:
The load-generator pod is consuming an abnormally high amount of CPU, triggering the high CPU usage alert. This high resource demand might lead to instability shown by previous OOM kills and restarts.

Suggested remediation:
- Investigate the load-generator workload configuration and resource limits to understand why it is consuming so much CPU.
- Adjust resource requests/limits to safeguard cluster stability.
- Review the load generation process or scale out load generators if needed to distribute the load.
- Monitor the pod's resource usage continuously to prevent further OOM kills or performance impacts.

Remaining uncertainty:
- The exact reason for extreme CPU usage by the load generator is unknown without deeper workload-specific logs or profiling.
- No error logs were found recently, so this appears more of a resource exhaustion issue than an explicit fault or failure.

This mostly indicates a resource demand issue with the load-generator pod causing the firing of the CPU high-rate alert.
